name: Lawley
bio: A soldier - Wilde believed a Third Hussars man - and a fellow prisoner in Reading, remembered by Wilde as "a quiet well-conducted chap in Reading always". In a postscript of June 1897 Wilde recommended him for a place in service, arguing that soldiers make good servants and that this one would make a good groom. **Even his name is uncertain**: the editors of the Complete Letters footnote it "Or possibly Langley", and nothing else about him survives - no first name, no dates, no outcome.
bio_note: From a postscript printed on p. 897, read at the rendered page.
